text:
One small fix in demo/pane.js, the live pane of the login demo (the workspace also holds demo/app/server.js, the little login app). Change only demo/pane.js: do not touch demo/app/server.js, create no other file in the workspace, and do not run git. Plain Node.js, built-in modules only, as before.

The problem
When the pane itself is stopped with SIGTERM or SIGINT in the middle of a check, it sends the app it started only SIGTERM and then exits at once. An app that ignores SIGTERM (for example one that installed a SIGTERM handler and is stuck in a busy loop) keeps running after the pane has gone. There is a second hole: a check removes its app from the set of running apps before it has finished stopping it, so a SIGTERM that reaches the pane while it is still waiting for that app to exit finds nothing to stop.

The fix
1. On SIGTERM or SIGINT the pane sends SIGKILL (not SIGTERM) to every app it has started and has not yet seen exit, and then exits at once.
2. An app stays in that set until it has really exited: take it out only after the code that stops it (SIGTERM, wait up to 1 second, then SIGKILL, then wait) has finished.
Keep everything else exactly as it is: the page, the checks, the timeouts and the usage rules.

How to test it, and where you may write
- The file tools may write only inside the workspace. Any scratch folder or scratch file goes under the directory named by the environment variable $TMPDIR and nowhere else: use the variable, never a path you typed yourself, and remove what you created there when you are done.
- In a scratch copy of demo/app make a server.js that installs a SIGTERM handler that does nothing and, when it gets a login request, spins forever in a busy loop. Start the pane on that folder, request the pane's page, and about 700 ms later send SIGTERM to the pane. Check that the pane exits within a second and that the scratch server.js process is gone within another second.
- Check that the pane on the real demo/app still shows the green welcome headline, and that no server.js or pane.js process of yours is left running at the end.
- If you cannot run something in this environment, say so plainly. Finish with a short summary of what you changed and what you tested.
Fixing the pane's shutdown so stuck apps can't outlive it.
Both edits are in — now putting the fix through its shutdown tests.

text: Generating a minimal server with no-op SIGTERM handler and a busy-loop login endpoint, then launching it in a pane.

args.description: Write stub server via shell to scratch

args.command:
cat > "$TMPDIR/runtest.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
SCRATCH="$TMPDIR/panetest-2"
PANE_PORT=45679
rm -f "$SCRATCH/pane.log" "$SCRATCH/page.out"
# start pane on stub folder
node demo/pane.js "$SCRATCH/appcopy" $PANE_PORT > "$SCRATCH/pane.log" 2>&1 &
PANE=$!
echo "pane pid $PANE"
# wait for pane listening
for i in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q "Pane listening" "$SCRATCH/pane.log" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
cat "$SCRATCH/pane.log"
# request page in background (check will hang on busy-loop login)
curl -s -m 15 "http://127.0.0.1:$PANE_PORT/" > "$SCRATCH/page.out" 2>"$SCRATCH/curl.err" &
CURLPID=$!
sleep 0.7
T0=$(date +%s%N)
kill -TERM $PANE
# wait up to 1s for pane exit
EXITED=""
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  if ! kill -0 $PANE 2>/dev/null; then EXITED=yes; break; fi
  sleep 0.05
done
T1=$(date +%s%N)
echo "pane-alive-after-1s: $(kill -0 $PANE 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo NO)"
echo "pane-exit-elapsed-ms: $(( (T1-T0)/1000000 ))"
wait $PANE 2>/dev/null; echo "pane wait exit: $?"
# check stub gone within another second
sleep 0.2
STUBPIDS=$(pgrep -f "appcopy/server.js" || true)
echo "stub pids right after pane exit: [$STUBPIDS]"
GONE=""
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  if [ -z "$(pgrep -f 'appcopy/server.js' || true)" ]; then GONE=yes; break; fi
  sleep 0.05
done
T2=$(date +%s%N)
echo "stub-gone-within-1s: ${GONE:-NO}"
echo "stub-wait-elapsed-ms: $(( (T2-T1)/1000000 ))"
echo "leftover stub pids: [$(pgrep -f 'appcopy/server.js' || true)]"
# cleanup strays
kill -KILL $CURLPID 2>/dev/null
wait 2>/dev/null
# kill any leftover stub hard
for p in $(pgrep -f 'appcopy/server.js' || true); do kill -KILL $p 2>/dev/null; done
kill -KILL $PANE 2>/dev/null
true
EOF
sh "$TMPDIR/runtest.sh"

What changed in `demo/pane.js`:
- `stopTrackedAppsAndExit` now sends `SIGKILL` (was `SIGTERM`) to every tracked app, then exits at once.
- `runCheck`'s `finally` now runs `await stopApp(child)` before `liveApps.delete(child)` (was delete-then-stop), so an app mid-shutdown stays in the set and still gets killed if the pane is signalled.

What I tested (all in one shell per test, scratch under `$TMPDIR`, removed afterwards):
- Stub test: scratch copy of `demo/app` with a `server.js` that ignores `SIGTERM` and busy-loops on login. Pane started on it, page requested, `SIGTERM` sent to the pane ~700 ms later. The stub was confirmed spinning (80% CPU, child of the pane). Pane exited in ~52 ms (within 1 s) and the stub was gone well within another second.
- Real app: pane on `demo/app` returned `<h1 class="ok">Welcome, Sam`, then pane stopped cleanly.
- Leftover check: no `node` processes remain (`ps -C node` empty).
